title: When News Left the Television: YouTube and the Rise of Small News Channels
excerpt: For decades, the news business operated on a simple assumption: if you wanted to reach a large audience, you needed a large organization. YouTube quietly disrupted that arrangement.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: UX Is Not UI Development: Defining the Modern UX Role
excerpt: Companies increasingly say they understand the importance of user experience, yet many still struggle to define what a UX Designer actually does. Somewhere between the hiring manager, recruiter and project team, UX has lost its definition.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: War at Machine Speed: AI, Human Judgment and the Future of Warfare
excerpt: War has always been a contest between human beings, but modern war is increasingly becoming a contest between systems. And somewhere inside this increasingly complicated machinery sits artificial intelligence, quietly changing one of the oldest human activities: the organisation of violence.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: When Agile Becomes the Enemy of UX
excerpt: Agile was supposed to make software development more human. Yet somewhere along the way, Agile became a process, and UX designers found themselves being asked to produce designs at the speed of a Jira ticket.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: UX Is Not a Cost Centre. Bad UX Is.
excerpt: There is a sentence that has quietly followed UX designers for years: “What is the ROI of UX?” Perhaps it is time to reverse the question: instead of asking what UX costs, ask what bad UX is costing the organization.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: When the River Takes the Economy With It: The Economic Cost of Floods in Assam
excerpt: Assam's floods do not simply destroy houses, roads and crops for a few days or weeks. They interrupt livelihoods, reduce household wealth, disrupt education, damage infrastructure, affect markets, increase public expenditure and push vulnerable families deeper into economic insecurity.
author: Jahangir Alam

title: A Taste of Assam: Culture, Memory and the Food of a Riverine Land

author: Jahangir Alam

title: Two Bengals, Two Tables: A Critical Reading of North Bengal and South Bengal Food Culture

author: Jahangir Alam
